title: Effectivity of formal systems of proper flat curves
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$, $n\geq1$, be objects of $\mathcal C(A/\mathfrak m^n)$, equipped with compatible isomorphisms $X_{n+1}\times_{A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}}A/\mathfrak m^n\cong X_n$. There is an object $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\mathcal C(A)$ and isomorphisms $X\times_AA/\mathfrak m^n\cong X_n$ compatible with all specified transition isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. The special fibre $X_1$ is proper and of finite type over $k$, hence separated. Its geometric fibre has dimension at most one by hypothesis. The field-extension dimension theorem gives $\dim|X_1|\leq1$. The schematicity theorem for separated algebraic spaces of dimension at most one therefore represents $X_1$ by a $k$-scheme. Its properness is the given properness, now for a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0E7R, proof, opening paragraph; geometric-to-ordinary dimension uses spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NS.

proof.text: Write the specified transition as $\tau_n:X_{n+1}\times_{S_{n+1}}S_n\xrightarrow{\sim}X_n$, where $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$. Define $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ as the base-change projection composed with $\tau_n^{-1}$. On every scheme chart of the target the quotient-base-change theorem identifies these maps with closed immersions defined by the extended quotient ideals. Thus they are representable closed immersions, and their composites identify $X_1$ with the closed subspace of $X_n$ defined by $\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X_n}$. This ideal is nilpotent, since $\mathfrak m^n=0$ on $X_n$. Thus $|X_1|\to|X_n|$ is a homeomorphism (on a scheme chart every prime contains a nilpotent ideal). The thickening theorem represents every $X_n$ by a scheme. Each remains proper and finitely presented over $A/\mathfrak m^n$. The scheme $X_1$, being finite type over a field, is Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem; therefore every $|X_n|$ is Noetherian and has dimension at most one.

source.place: Tag 0E7R, proof, paragraph beginning with the lifting of L_1 and its observation that all X_n are schemes.

proof.text: The proper scheme $X_1$ of dimension at most one is projective over $k$. Choose a closed immersion $X_1\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ supplied by that theorem. Pulling back $\mathcal O(1)$ along it gives an ample invertible module $\mathcal L_1$ on $X_1$, including when $X_1$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 0A26 (lemma-dim-1-proper-projective), as used in Tag 0E7R; properties.tex Tags 01PS and 01PU for the ample module.

proof.text: Inductively suppose $\mathcal L_n$ has been chosen. Since $X_{n+1}$ has Noetherian underlying space of dimension at most one, the Picard lifting theorem applied to the closed immersion $i_n$ supplies an invertible $\mathcal L_{n+1}$ and an isomorphism $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal L_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_n$. Begin with the ample $\mathcal L_1$ of step 3 and choose such a pair at each integer stage. For $a<b$ put $i_{a,b}=i_{b-1}\circ\cdots\circ i_a$. Set $i_{a,a}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi_{a,a}=\mathrm{id}$, and recursively define $\varphi_{a,b+1}=\varphi_{a,b}\circ i_{a,b}^*\varphi_b:i_{a,b+1}^*\mathcal L_{b+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_a$, using the canonical identification of iterated pullbacks. Associativity of composition gives $\varphi_{a,c}=\varphi_{a,b}\circ i_{a,b}^*\varphi_{b,c}$ for $a\leq b\leq c$, by induction on $c-b$. Thus these choices give a compatible system, including all nonadjacent restrictions. The cited algebraization theorem requires ampleness only of $\mathcal L_1$; no ampleness claim at higher stages is used.

source.place: Tag 09NY (lemma-lift-line-bundle-from-reduction-dimension-1); this carries the obstruction-vanishing argument in Tag 0E7R.

proof.text: Apply polarized formal algebraization with $I=\mathfrak m$ to the cartesian scheme system and $(\mathcal L_n,\varphi_n)$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian and complete, $X_1$ is proper, and $\mathcal L_1$ is ample. It gives a proper scheme $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and base-linear isomorphisms $a_n:X_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_n$, where $Y_n=X\times_A A/\mathfrak m^n$. If $j_n:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ is the quotient inclusion, the cited statement gives $a_{n+1}\circ i_n=j_n\circ a_n$. Set $\alpha_n=a_n^{-1}$. Multiplying this equality by the inverses gives $i_n\circ\alpha_n=\alpha_{n+1}\circ j_n$. Let $\beta_n:Y_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_{n+1}\times_{S_{n+1}}S_n$ be the canonical base-change isomorphism. By the fibre-product universal property the preceding equality says exactly $\tau_n\circ(\alpha_{n+1}\times_{S_{n+1}}S_n)\circ\beta_n=\alpha_n$: the projections agree because $i_n$ was defined through $\tau_n^{-1}$. Composing these identities verifies compatibility between any two stages. Thus the reductions are identified as the given formal system, not just individually. Properness gives finite type, quasi-compactness and separatedness. The locally finite-type morphism $f$ over the locally Noetherian base is locally of finite presentation by the cited theorem. Separatedness gives quasi-separatedness by the cited lemma; these three clauses give finite presentation by its definition.

Work on an affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ with $B$ a finite-type $A$-algebra. The Noetherian permanence theorem makes $B$ Noetherian. By the quotient-base-change theorem its reduction $V_n=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak m^nB)$ is an affine open of $X\times_AA/\mathfrak m^n$, hence of $X_n$ via $\alpha_n$. The given flatness of $X_n$ and the affine flatness criterion show that $B/\mathfrak m^nB$ is flat over $A/\mathfrak m^n$ for every $n\geq1$. Apply the flat-module-powers theorem with $(R,S,I,M)=(A,B,\mathfrak m,B)$; $B$ is generated by $1$ as a $B$-module. It follows that $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat for every prime $\mathfrak q$ containing $\mathfrak mB$; by the affine-open stalk theorem $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is the local ring of $X$ at the corresponding point. Since $A$ is local, these points are precisely the points of $V$ over its closed point. Thus all stalks on the closed fibre are flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0D4G (lemma-check-flatness-on-infinitesimal-nbhds), its affine translation via algebra.tex Tag 0523.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq X$ be the set where the stalk is flat as an $A$-module; on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ the stalk at $\mathfrak q$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$ by the affine-open stalk theorem. On each finite-type affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the Noetherian flat-neighborhood theorem with $M=B$ makes this set open. The equivalence of flatness over $A$ and over its localization at the image prime identifies $U$ with the flat locus of $f$. It contains the whole closed fibre by the preceding step. Its complement $C$ is closed; since $f$ is a closed map by properness, $f(C)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and misses $\mathfrak m$. A nonempty closed set $V(J)$ in a local spectrum contains $\mathfrak m$, since every proper ideal $J$ lies in $\mathfrak m$. Hence $f(C)=\varnothing$, so $C=\varnothing$ and $f$ is flat everywhere.

source.place: Tag 0D58 proof, globalization of the flatness assertion after Tag 0D4G; openness from algebra.tex Tag 00RC, Noetherian case.

proof.text: For the proper scheme morphism $f$, the set $W=\{s:\dim X_s\leq1\}$ is open by upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension. It contains the closed point because its fibre is $X_1$. Every open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak m$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the whole spectrum: it contains some $D(a)$ with $a\notin\mathfrak m$, and such $a$ is a unit. Consequently every ordinary fibre has dimension at most one. Each fibre is proper by the proper-base-change theorem, hence a separated finite-type scheme over its residue field, so the field-extension dimension theorem shows the same bound for every geometric fibre. Thus $X$ is an object of $\mathcal C(A)$. The already constructed $\alpha_n$ supply all requested compatible identifications.

lean.statement: theorem formal_effectivity (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] (X : ∀ n : ℕ, ProperCurveFamily (effectivityBase A n)) (i : ∀ n : ℕ, (X n).space.obj.obj ⟶ (X (n + 1)).space.obj.obj) (hcart : ∀ n : ℕ, IsPullback (i n) (X n).projection (X (n + 1)).projection (yoneda.map (effectivityBaseStep A n))) : ∃ Y : ProperCurveFamily (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of A)))), ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ, pullback Y.projection (yoneda.map (effectivityBaseι A n)) ≅ (X n).space.obj.obj, (∀ n : ℕ, (e n).hom ≫ (X n).projection = pullback.snd Y.projection (yoneda.map (effectivityBaseι A n))) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, (e n).inv ≫ pullback.fst Y.projection (yoneda.map (effectivityBaseι A n)) = i n ≫ (e (n + 1)).inv ≫ pullback.fst Y.projection (yoneda.map (effectivityBaseι A (n + 1))))
